According to Norton et al. (1993), the Rickettsiales-like infections wiped out almost 94.5% of juvenile cultured giant clams. This is particularly important as species is bred for restocking purposes, and overcrowding and lack of water turnover rates increase the infection rates. It is therefore unwise to translocate clams infected with these organisms to new regions/countries, or back to the wild.
